name: Battle of the Nile

phases.title: The French line at anchor, the British closing
phases.text: The French thirteen ships of the line lay at anchor along the edge of the shoals, with the van near Aboukir Island and Orient at the centre. The British fleet came up in the evening, with Swiftsure and Alexander out of sight to the west.

phases.title: Goliath and Zealous cross the head of the line
phases.text: Foley saw a gap between Guerrier and the shoal and took Goliath through it, and Zealous followed. Orion, Theseus and Audacious also passed inside the line, which was ready to fight only on its seaward side.

phases.title: The seaward ships anchor and the centre is engaged
phases.text: Vanguard, Minotaur and Defence anchored on the seaward side of the French van at 18:40, which was now caught on both sides. Bellerophon and Majestic passed the melee and went on to the unengaged French centre.

phases.title: Culloden runs onto the shoal
phases.text: Culloden, the last ship of the British line, sailed too close to Aboukir Island in the growing darkness and stuck fast on the shoal. Her boats, the brig Mutine and Leander could not move her.

phases.title: Bellerophon drifts out and the last ships join
phases.text: Bellerophon, battered by Orient, cut her anchor cables at 20:20 and drifted away from the fight. Swiftsure and Alexander came up in the dark and opened fire on Orient and Franklin.

phases.title: The French van surrenders
phases.text: Guerrier, Conquérant and Spartiate struck their colours, and Aquilon was dismasted and its officers surrendered at 21:25. Peuple Souverain had already cut its cable and drifted south, and surrendered in the night.

phases.title: Fire breaks out on Orient
phases.text: A fire was seen on Orient's lower decks and Swiftsure fired into the blaze, which spread through the stern. The nearest British ships edged away, and Tonnant, Heureux and Mercure cut their cables and drifted south.

phases.title: Orient explodes
phases.text: At 22:00 the fire reached the magazines and Orient was destroyed by a massive explosion. Flaming wreckage fell over the nearest ships, and for ten minutes afterwards there was no firing.

phases.title: Franklin fights on and surrenders
phases.text: Franklin restarted the engagement by firing on Swiftsure. Isolated and battered, she was dismasted, and the wounded Blanquet surrendered to the combined fire of Swiftsure and Defence.

phases.title: Tonnant fights on alone and drifts south
phases.text: By midnight only Tonnant remained engaged, fighting Majestic until about 03:00, when she was a dismasted hulk. She then drifted southwards away from the action towards Villeneuve's division.

phases.title: Firing begins again at dawn
phases.text: As the sun rose, firing broke out again between the French southern division and the battered Alexander and Majestic.

phases.title: Heureux and Mercure surrender on the shoal
phases.text: Heureux and Mercure had cut their cables to escape the exploding Orient and had drifted onto the shoal. Alexander and three other British ships attacked them, and both surrendered within minutes.

phases.title: Tonnant is driven ashore and the French rear stands out
phases.text: Villeneuve brought most of the surviving French ships to the mouth of the bay at 11:00. The dismasted Tonnant could not make the speed and was driven ashore by her crew, while the others stood out to sea.

note: A battle at sea, drawn as a schematic: the real line was about 2,850 yards long and the plan is not to scale. The four French frigates of the inner line, the bomb vessels and the brigs are not drawn, and the shoals are shown in the land colour. Peuple Souverain is drawn inside the French van: it cut its cable and drifted south, but the accounts do not say where it stopped, and it surrendered in the night. Leander and Timoléon are not drawn as formations: Timoléon was part of the French rear and grounded on the shoal. Swiftsure and Alexander are drawn as one block, as are the five ships that passed inside the line. The accounts do not say where Bellerophon drifted to.
